newsitem.title: USA: Merck rises as analysts boost estimates.
newsitem.headline: Merck rises as analysts boost estimates.

text.p: Merck and Co Inc's share price rose Thursday after analysts raised their earnings estimates on the pharmaceutical company and the firm unveiled an animal health joint venture with Rhone-Poulenc SA.

Analysts linked much of the stock's rise to an upbeat meeting with analysts Wednesday at which company executives said Merck expected 1996 fourth quarter and full-year 1997 earnings to be at the top of the range of estimates.
Analysts also said the animal health joint venture would help Merck get the most out of that business.
"I think it's a followthrough from the earnings" comment on Wednesday, NatWest Securities analyst Edward Pykon said of Merck's share price rise.
The stock, a Dow Industrials component, was up 2-5/8 to 79-1/2. Merck rose 5/8 to 76-7/8 Wednesday, closing off its session high of 78-1/4.

Merck on Wednesday said it expected fourth quarter earnings to be at the top of analysts' estimates of $0.80 to $0.86 a share, and its 1997 earnings to be at the top of estimates of $3.55 to $3.75 a share.
Merck executives also said Wednesday that they expect the company's lineup of new drugs to offset patent expirations of key moneymakers coming at the end of the decade.
Salomon Brothers analyst Robert Uhl boosted his 1997 esrnings estimate on Merck to $3.75 a share from $3.65.

Deutsche Morgan Grenfell analyst Mariola Haggar raised her 1996 estimate "preliminarily" to $3.20 a share from $3.17. She raised her 1997 estimate to $3.80 from $3.65 and boosted her five-year compound earnings per share growth rate to 17 percent from 15 percent.
Analysts praised the deal between French chemical group Rhone-Poulenc and Merck.
"The two together are far stronger," Uhl said.
Analysts cited the combined benefit of Merck's strong U.S. sales presence and Rhone-Poulenc's strength in Europe and other international markets.

Aros Securities analyst David Maris said the joint venture will give Merck's animal health sales force added products to combine with its flagship animal drug Invermectin, for treating animal parasites. The drug had sales of $520 million in the first nine months of 1996.
"It's leveraging Merck's great presence in animal health," Maris said.
